sections.h2: Burke County Tax Office contact and divisions
sections.html:
The Tax Office works out of the Burke Services Building, 110 North Green Street, Morganton, NC 28655, from 8 am until 5 pm each weekday. The phone is (828) 764-9430, letters go to PO Box 219, Morganton, NC 28680, and Collections takes email at collections@burkenc.org.

Three divisions split the work. Real Property appraises land and buildings and answers questions on values, revaluation and appeals. Personal and Business Property takes listings and forms for taxable equipment and business assets. Collections issues bills and accepts payment for the county plus the towns and fire districts the office serves, so one bill can carry several levies.

The office also publishes its deed certification form and a tax website at burkenctax.com. If you are selling, start with Collections, the division that certifies the amount owed on a parcel before a deed moves on to recording.

Burke's own levy is 55.5 cents per $100 of assessed value, and the budget for fiscal 2026-2027, about $120.7 million, kept it there. That budget began July 1, 2026. The county has cut the rate twice since 2023.

Your bill may list more than the county line, because town and fire district charges go through the same office. Look at each rate line for the units covering your address. A rate multiplies a value, and values will shift once the 2027 revaluation project is done.

Burke County is carrying out a revaluation project for 2027. Commissioners hold a public hearing at the Burke Services Building on a proposed Schedule of Values and Present Use Schedule of Values, with copies posted online and at the tax office. Call the Tax Department at (828) 764-9430 with questions about the schedules.

State law (G.S. 105-286) sets an eight-year ceiling between reappraisals, each as of January 1. Larger counties, those with 75,000 residents or more, can be forced to reappraise early if their sales assessment ratio drops below .85 or climbs above 1.15. The review board gets until December 1 in a revaluation year, a longer runway than usual.

When your new notice comes, set it beside recent sales of comparable homes nearby before deciding whether to appeal.

Bills fall due on September 1, with face-amount payment allowed until January 6.

Statutory dates in a Burke County tax year
EventDate or rule
Listing windowStarts on the first business day of January and ends January 31
Bill duePayable September 1 of the fiscal year
Face-amount paymentPayment received ahead of January 6
First interest step2% on balances from January 6 to February 1
Ongoing interest3/4 of 1% for every month or part, after February 1
Review board opensNo sooner than the first Monday in April and no later than the first Monday in May
State-level appealNotice due within 30 days of the board's mailed decision

Each summer the county mails listing forms for owners to update, sign and send back. Returning them within the January window avoids a late listing penalty.

Talk to the Tax Office first. Anything unresolved goes to the review board, which is the commissioners unless the county has formed a special panel. Your request must be in hand before the panel adjourns.

  • A written request or a personal appearance both count.
  • If the board's own notice was mailed less than 15 days before adjourning, the clock gives you 15 days from that mailing.
  • The ruling arrives by mail within 30 days after adjournment.
  • Past that sits the Property Tax Commission, which takes a written notice listing your grounds, with a copy to the assessor.

If your house has unrepaired storm damage, tell the Tax Office. Ask what relief is open to your parcel now.

sections.h2: Certification required before a deed is recorded
sections.html:
Burke uses a Delinquent Tax Certification form built on G.S. 161-31, which lets commissioners instruct the register of deeds to turn away a transfer deed until the collector certifies there are no delinquent taxes. The form was revised April 22, 2026.

You supply the parcel number, the seller and buyer names, the buyer's mailing address, the site address, the price and the acreage. The form also asks if a mobile home or personal property, such as vehicles, boats or farm equipment, goes with the sale, and whether land in Present Use Value will stay enrolled. Staff then complete a ten-year grid of deferred and due taxes.

Send it to the Office of the Tax Administrator, PO Box 219, Morganton, or to collections@burkenc.org. A closing attorney often files it, though asking Collections for a figure before you list can save days.

The state's three programs apply here, filed on Form AV-9 with the county assessor, and applications must be accepted through June 1. An owner may draw on one program only.

  • Elderly or disabled exclusion: removes whichever is greater, $25,000 or half the appraised value of a permanent residence, for an owner at least 65 or totally and permanently disabled whose prior-year income stays within the 2026 cap of $38,800.
  • Disabled veteran exclusion: the first $45,000 of appraised value, with no age or income test.
  • Circuit breaker: tax limited to 4% of income, or 5% where income runs up to $58,200, once the owner has lived in the home five years.

Circuit breaker savings are deferred, and the tax deferred over the three prior years falls due on a transfer, an owner's death or a move out. Mention any such deferral to your closing attorney.

sections.h2: Selling a Burke County home: tax steps
sections.html:
Begin by calling Collections at (828) 764-9430 for the amount owed on the parcel, including any town or fire district levy. Next, decide who will file the Delinquent Tax Certification. Your closing attorney usually does, but you can send it yourself to PO Box 219 or collections@burkenc.org with the parcel number, the buyer and seller names, the price and the acreage.

If land is in Present Use Value, say whether the buyer will keep it enrolled, since the form asks. If you have a circuit breaker deferral, expect the deferred tax from the three prior years to come due at the sale. Once the collector certifies that nothing delinquent remains, the register of deeds can accept the deed.

Growth is slow. The mid-2025 population is 88,655, up just 1.2% from the 2020 base and below the 90,912 counted in 2010. The county has 41,669 housing units, and 74.5% of homes are owner-occupied with a median value of $185,400. Median gross rent is $884, and 588 building permits were issued in 2025. At that price level, back taxes or a certification delay can hold up a closing, so ask Collections for your balance early.

faqs.q: What is Burke County's rate per $100?
faqs.a: It is 55.5 cents, unchanged for 2026-2027, plus any town or fire district charges that reach your parcel.

faqs.q: Where can I pay a Burke County bill?
faqs.a: Go to 110 North Green Street in Morganton during weekday office hours, call (828) 764-9430, or email collections@burkenc.org.

faqs.q: When does interest start on Burke County bills?
faqs.a: Interest starts January 6, since payment before that date is at face amount. It is 2% through February 1 and 3/4 of 1% a month after.
Yes, a 2027 revaluation is under way, and state law demands reappraisal at least every eighth year. Call the Tax Department at (828) 764-9430 about the proposed schedules.

faqs.q: Do I need tax certification to sell in Burke County?
faqs.a: Yes, the county's Delinquent Tax Certification lets the collector confirm nothing delinquent remains before the deed goes on record. Request it at collections@burkenc.org or (828) 764-9430.
